question.worked_solution:
First, we let

$$
I=\int \frac{{ln}^{8}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{8}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{8{ln}^{7}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{x}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{8}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{8}⁡x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)(\frac{8{ln}^{7}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{9}⁡x-8\int \frac{{ln}^{8}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{9}⁡x-8I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $I,$ remembering to add a constant of integration $C$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={ln}^{9}⁡x-8I \\ 9I & ={ln}^{9}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{9}⁡x}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$
